properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-23: *"the other idea was just making dynograph-foundation a set of semi independent crates that you just pick what you like from? this is really a dynograph-foundation issue, I'm asking it here"*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ THE FIRST HALF IS ALREADY TRUE, MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-08-23

dynograph-foundation holds **TEN crates**: `client`, `cluster`, `core`, `game`, `graph`, `resolution`, `service`, `storage`, `text`, `vector`.

**reflow2 already picks five of them** — `core`, `storage`, `graph`, `resolution`, `vector` — and declines `client`, `cluster`, `game` and `service` outright. `text` is not taken directly at all; it is reached only through `dynograph-storage`'s optional `fulltext` feature. And `storage` is taken with `default-features = false`, with `rocksdb` and `fulltext` opted into by name in `crates/reflow2-core/Cargo.toml`.

⭐ So "a set of semi-independent crates you pick what you like from" IS WHAT IT ALREADY IS, at the crate level and at the feature level. `dynograph-game` and `dynograph-service` existing while reflow2 has never heard of them is the proposal already working — and `service` is almost certainly the REST surface storyflow consumes, which makes `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface` visible in the file layout.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📐 THE RESIDUAL: INDEPENDENT IN CODE, COUPLED IN RELEASE

All five are pinned in reflow2's `Cargo.toml` as:

    { git = "https://github.com/sligara7/dynograph-foundation.git", tag = "v0.12.0" }

**One repo, one tag, five crates.** You can pick WHICH CRATES you take; you cannot pick WHICH VERSION of each. They are not published to crates.io — the workspace comment says so — which is also why the `[patch."https://…"]` block exists, commented out, for local cross-repo development.

⭐⭐ **AND THERE IS A WORKED EXAMPLE ALREADY IN THE GRAPH.** `fact:dynograph-v0130-measured-clean-and-the-pin-is-parked` records that v0.13.0's `git diff v0.12.0 v0.13.0` over ALL SIX crates reflow2 touches is **EMPTY** — the entire release changed only `dynograph-client` and `dynograph-service`, neither of which reflow2 depends on. **A release that provably could not affect reflow2 still cost a session to confirm**, across four independent grounds and a full `cargo test --workspace`, and the pin bump is still PARKED awaiting Anthony's word.

⇒ That is precisely the cost of coupling release to repository rather than to crate, stated in a real measurement rather than as an argument. **The question is not "should they be separate crates" — they are. It is "should they be separately RELEASABLE".** A much smaller question than the idea sounds like, and a different one from absorbing anything.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, UNRANKED, each with what it costs

**A. LEAVE IT — one repo, one tag, pick your crates.** The status quo, and already most of what was asked for.
   ⭐ The monolithic tag is not only a cost: the five crates are always mutually consistent, and reflow2 has never had to reason about a version matrix. `reflow2.toml`'s pin carries a written reason for every bump (v0.11.0 → v0.12.0 closed a type leak) — and ONE pin is what makes that note writable at all.
   ⚠️ A consumer who wants one crate takes the release cadence of all ten, and pays a confirmation session for releases that cannot touch it.

**B. VERSION THE CRATES INDEPENDENTLY WITHIN THE REPO** — per-crate versions or tags under one repository.
   ⚠️ Independent versions mean a compatibility matrix somebody maintains and tests. `dynograph-storage` re-exports `dynograph_core::Value` — reflow2 imports `dynograph_storage::Value` in two places — so core and storage are not independently versionable in any real sense without a stated compatibility contract between them.

**C. PUBLISH TO crates.io.** Turns "pick what you like" from a git-tag arrangement into the ordinary Rust one, and removes the `[patch]` dance.
   ⚠️ Publishing is a commitment: names are permanent, yanks are loud, and a pre-1.0 foundation currently free to move acquires an audience. Same shape as `designation: published` on an Interface — publishing is a promise, not a distribution mechanism.

**D. SPLIT THE REPO** — one repository per crate, or per cluster.
   ⚠️ The heaviest option, and it multiplies the release ceremony reflow2 has just spent a session documenting. Ten repos with ten release cuts to keep coherent is a worse problem than one tag.

**E. CHANGE NOTHING UPSTREAM; LET reflow2 STOP TAKING WHAT IT BARELY USES.** `dynograph_resolution` is one function and `dynograph_vector` is two — both absorbable by reflow2 (option C of `dec:idea-cannibalize-dynograph-foundation-into-reflow2`) with no upstream change at all.
   ⭐ The only option here reflow2 can act on unilaterally, in its own repo, without a decision about somebody else's project.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 THE HONEST BOUND, and it is about ownership rather than engineering

**Nothing here has been discussed with dynograph-foundation as a project, and reflow2's design has no standing to decide it.** Four of the ten crates exist for consumers reflow2 knows nothing about — `game` and `cluster` are not reflow2's business, and a change made to suit reflow2's consumption pattern could be wrong for whoever uses those. The only options reflow2 can weigh honestly on its own are **A** (accept it) and **E** (take less).

**AND THE SEPARATE FINDING WORTH KEEPING WHATEVER IS DECIDED:** this node lives in reflow2's graph while being about another system, and only its prose says so. That is the gap, not the workaround.
properties.name: OPEN — dynograph-foundation's crates are already pickable; should they become independently RELEASABLE, so a consumer can pin one without pinning all five?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Anthony, 2026-08-23, raising a second option beside the absorb idea.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⏸️ PARTIALLY ANSWERED, 2026-08-23, AND THE PART THAT WAS NOT ANSWERED MATTERS MORE.

His words, in the same breath as deferring the absorption: *"okay, let's leave dynograph-foundation as its own repo for now. defer absorbing into reflow2."*

**WHAT THAT SETTLES: option D (split the repo) is off, and option A (leave it) stands FOR NOW.** "As its own repo" is explicit.

🛑 **WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, stated so the deferral is not read wider than it is:** options **B** (version the crates independently within the repo) and **C** (publish to crates.io) were never put to him and he said nothing about either. Staying "its own repo" is compatible with both — per-crate tags and a crates.io release both live inside one repository. So the RELEASABILITY question this node is named for is **still open**, and the status stays `proposed` for that reason rather than by neglect.

⚠️ AND IT REMAINS NOT REFLOW2'S TO DECIDE. The ownership bound in the decision text is unchanged: four of the ten crates serve consumers reflow2 knows nothing about, and only options A and E can be weighed honestly from here.

⭐ THE OPTION THAT SURVIVED INTACT IS **E** — reflow2 absorbing `token_sort_ratio`, `mean` and `linear_regression_slope` and taking less. It needs no upstream decision at all. It was put to him as the recommendation on the sibling node and DEFERRED there too, so it is waiting, not dead.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THIS DECISION GOVERNS ANOTHER REPOSITORY. Its subject is `dynograph-foundation`, not reflow2. It is recorded in reflow2's graph because that is where he asked it, because dynograph-foundation has no reflow2 design of its own — and because NOTHING IN THE SCHEMA RECORDS WHICH REPO A DECISION GOVERNS, so only this prose says so. That gap was filed independently by a dev_storyflow session on 2026-08-17 (item ④): a design question about another repo has nowhere of its own to live. **No work is to be done in that repository on the strength of this node.**

DEDUP: read four near-matches in full. Distinct from `dec:idea-cannibalize-dynograph-foundation-into-reflow2` (what the CONSUMER does) because this asks what the SUPPLIER should be; from the rejected swap idea (reimplementation); from `dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier` (what it IS in reflow2's model); and from `fact:dynograph-v0130-measured-clean-and-the-pin-is-parked`, which is a measured observation about one release rather than a question about release structure — though it turned out to be this node's sharpest supporting evidence, so it is cited rather than restated.
